thesis: The market treats a CPI print as a direction event and hedges it with index exposure, which is why every vol-crush cell around this print has been arbitraged flat and why one died in this morning's checks. What is left is a dispersion effect nobody is positioned for. Across the 311 CPI eves since 2000 the Nasdaq has beaten the S&P by 11.5 basis points over the print session alone once the pair is hedged for beta, winning 59.8% of the time and in 22 of 27 calendar years. The other side is index-level hedging demand: desks manage event risk in the most liquid instrument they have, which pushes the broad index around on the print session while the rate-sensitive half of the tape reprices on the number itself, and a beta-matched pair collects the gap without taking a side on the number. The tell that this is structural rather than a momentum artifact is the direction split, because the equal-dollar version of the same spread makes its money only when SPY rallies and loses when SPY falls, while the beta-matched version does its best work on down sessions.

evidence.summary: Long QQQ against a beta-matched short SPY, sized at 1.48 dollars of SPY per dollar of QQQ from the point-in-time 126-day beta, entered MOC on the session before a CPI release and exited MOC on the print session. N=311 eves 2000-2026: mean +0.115% of the QQQ leg, hit 59.8%, t 2.76, sign p 0.00032, bootstrap P(mean<=0) 0.0036, and +0.108pp of excess over the spread's own all-days drift. The anchor is specific to CPI, since the identical construction pays -0.002% on PPI eves, -0.041% on NFP eves, +0.065% on FOMC eves and +0.007% on all days. It replicates on the underlying price indices with no ETF involved (^NDX against ^GSPC, +0.097%, 60.5% hit, sign p 0.00014) and survives every hedge definition tested, spanning +0.099% to +0.127% across 63, 126 and 252-day betas and two volatility-ratio hedges. Edge is 11.5 bps against a pair round trip of roughly 1 to 2 bps in the two most liquid ETFs listed, so this is a reliability trade rather than a size trade: at 30 bps the position is 20.5% of NAV gross, net market exposure is 0.02% of NAV, and the worst session in 26 years would have cost 0.22% of NAV. Computed fresh this morning against the 2026-08-10 close.
evidence.control: the spread's own all-days drift of +0.007% over the same one-session horizon; three placebo event anchors (PPI eve -0.002%, NFP eve -0.041%, FOMC eve +0.065%); and the equal-dollar construction of the same pair, which pays +0.085% and is the version that fails

title: Own the long end from tonight's inflation close into tomorrow's producer print

exit.event_anchor: exit on the close of the PPI print session itself, 2026-08-13

thesis: Tonight's close carries a risk premium for two inflation prints, not one. When CPI and PPI land on consecutive sessions the market prices the pair as a single block, and the duration holder gets paid to sit through the second, lower-information half of it: the PPI session pays TLT +25.8 bps when a CPI printed on its eve against +8.4 bps when one did not, and the session immediately before the print pays nothing at all. The other side is whoever bought protection across the block and unwinds it once the headline number is out, plus the rates shorts positioned for a producer print that almost never moves the story after CPI has. Consensus treats PPI as a footnote, which is the reason the premium survives to be collected. 95% of the payoff arrives in the 08:30 gap, so this is a one-session release trade and nothing else.

evidence.summary: PPI print session whose eve carried a CPI print, long TLT close to close: +25.8 bps raw, +22.2 bps against a trading-day-of-month matched control, record 35-20 (63.6% hit) against TLT's 52.1% unconditional base rate, bootstrap P(mean<=0) 0.034. The same print session without a CPI on its eve pays +5.6 bps excess at 55.5%, and the offset ladder is a one-session spike rather than a plateau (k=-1 -10.6 bps, the trade +25.8 bps, k=+1 -5.7 bps). Charged in full for the August month effect the honest expectation is +16.0 bps against a 2.6 bps all-in round trip, roughly 6x cost. 8 of 11 years positive with no single year carrying it (best 2025 +0.884% on N=5, 2020 +0.618% on N=7).
evidence.control: trading-day-of-month matched TLT drift, because a rates event cell measured against an all-days control is invalid: TLT's own unconditional return swings from -0.202% at tdom 2 to +0.215% at tdom 14 with no event anywhere. Cross-checked against a month x tdom double control, which reads +24.7 bps at a 69.1% hit.
evidence.era_note: 52 of 55 observations are 2018 or later, and that is by construction rather than a selected era: back-to-back CPI-then-PPI scheduling is a modern BLS calendar artifact. The cell therefore has one regime and can never have a second, which is why it is graded B and not A.

A green gap fully retraced by 11:00 ET means the premium already released and the session has turned into a rates repricing this trade has no edge in.

reason: Twelve candidates were selected off the surface map across ten asset classes, and eleven died. The event lane was the productive one because today is simultaneously a CPI print and a PPI eve, but its other four expressions all failed: the vehicle translations into IEF and LQD carry no separate mechanism and LQD does not clear its own cost, the spread against SPY adds a leg with negative beta that doubles the bet without adding alpha, and the two commodity and volatility inversions on the same anchor were both beaten by nonsense placebo anchors. The price-state lane came back empty in a coherent way: every one of the four candidates, plus the two the watchlist explicitly owed a check, died on a conditioner that is live today rather than on their headline numbers. Utilities inverted under the SPY-near-high gate that is on, the semis laggard turned out to select tape 35 points more bearish than base rate while today's SMH sits 25% above its 200d, the skew divergence was carried entirely by the not-midterm and not-near-high complement, and the Brazil washout was 71% two episodes. The metals complex was dismissed before its numbers mattered because a live GDX leg runs to 08-17 and the registry rule on correlated second legs applies. One idea is what survived, and padding to three would have meant shipping something already measured as dead.

Twelve directions across ten cells and seven asset classes, and the market answered the same way in three different accents: the anchor was decoration, the gate did not filter, or the vehicle ate the edge. The two calendar cells the window actually offered, VIX-expiry week and the August pre-opex run, were already swept and dead in the registry, so they were dismissed on their own numbers rather than re-tested. Of what was left, the Jackson Hole legs turned out to be an August month-of-year seasonal wearing an event label (the unconditional Aug 6-16 window pays +1.025% at t=6.90 and thirteen placebo offsets beat the real anchor), the 98th-percentile contango cell is a lagging marker of a short-vol run that has already happened, the macro vacuum is the FOMC exclusion re-labeled, and the fragility dial's rate of change flips sign on its own threshold, its own lookback and its own vintage. One idea reached development and then died to the reference class, which is the honest reason nothing ships: run its rule across 27 sector ETFs and the cross-section is statistically homogeneous at exactly zero.

VIX expiry is today, opex is Friday and Jackson Hole is seven sessions out, and this repo has swept and killed all three, Jackson Hole across five asset classes as recently as yesterday. Four separate cells died to the same shape: the condition that made the candidate interesting turned out to subtract from the plain state underneath it. The crude-at-a-floor gate takes energy at a 52-week high from +0.606% to -1.465%; the momentum-turn gate takes a deep drawdown from +0.470% to -0.282%; the index-near-a-high gate takes a megacap washout down by 0.306pp; and the two gates defining the semis-break cell move its number by 0.004pp. The rotation trade itself was the closest thing to a real finding and it is 96% two 2026 prints. Eleven candidates over five axes and nine asset classes, twenty-eight check scripts, and nothing reached the bar. Three came close enough to be worth writing down, and each died to a different test. The morning had two genuinely unexamined surfaces and both came back empty: the opex anchor crossed with every non-equity class (gold, silver, duration, credit, energy, the dollar and China, a hundred cells whose excess standard deviation is 0.132pp with not one cell clearing a percentage point), and Jackson Hole on the two classes its five-class sweep never reached. That JH work turned up the structural fact that decides both: the August opex close IS the JH-5 anchor in 21 of 26 years, so the two lanes were one anchor family wearing two labels, and both labels were already closed. Of the twenty-one live watchlist entries, one fired all of its stated conditions for the first time and still died, on a trend-state rung the entry never encoded. The tape offered no shortage of extremes to work with, but today's specific readings sat on the wrong side of the cells that pay: gold thrusting from sixteen percent below its high rather than near it, silver deeper in drawdown than any historical anchor, energy at a fifty-two week high where the parked crude entry's own condition forbids the trade, and a midterm year that inverts the one index cell with a strong parent.

title: Buy the first flush inside a parabolic gold-miner run

thesis: GDX has run 38.0% in 21 sessions, a 99.6th-percentile thrust on its own trailing year, and on Tuesday it fell 2.94%. Most of the tape reads a violent down day inside a parabolic run as the top, and this book is built to read it that way: three of its fifteen strategies are overbought fades, and the ledger carries 53 Overbot Vol Spike shorts inside these historical windows averaging -0.36R. The six prior instances since 2008 say the flush is where leveraged holders get cleared while the underlying bid stays, paying +5.75% over the next five sessions against GDX's own +0.27% drift over the same span, 6 for 6. The same rule run on four single-name miners replicates at 22-8 with a sign-test p of 0.012 against their own up-rate, so this is not one ETF's quirk. The seller on a one-day move like this is margin and levered-ETF rebalancing, and neither of those has a view on gold.

The dose response grades correctly across three independent rank rungs and today's -2.94% sits at +5.104% (3-0) on the live >=99 rung. Honest expectation is the family-shrunk number rather than the headline: the same rule on NEM, AEM, AU and KGC pools to +2.228% over 30 episodes, so 2-3% is the number to plan around, not 5.75%. Cost is 109x a 5 bp GDX round trip even on the shrunk estimate.

reason: The placebo offset ladder, then gate attribution, then the cycle. The ladder at h=5 runs ME-5 +1.416% at t 2.79, ME-4 +0.614%, ME-3 +0.491%, and the pitched ME-1 entry at +0.008% and t 0.02, so the proposed anchor sits at the bottom of its own ladder and the three-sector form is a flat plateau with every t below 1.6, which is calendar position wearing an event label. The washout conditioner makes things worse rather than better: the bare ME-1 month turn pays +0.105% on 319 observations, the conditioned cell +0.008% on 35, and simply owning the basket every day pays +0.175%. The midterm cell is wrong-signed at -0.773% on 13 observations at t -2.11 and a 30.8% hit, an eighth reproduction of the inversion, in exactly the year we would trade. The 110-cell grid's best occupant survives a Sidak correction at only p 0.358.

Twenty-two candidates across ten asset classes and six novelty axes, and every one died on a substantive number rather than on a thin record. The scheduled 5:10 run executed, wrote eleven candidates into today's folder and then died before publishing, so this is a re-run that inherits its work and adjudicates the one cell it left open. The shape of the morning is now six sessions old and the registry has been right about it every time: with Jackson Hole closed on eight classes pre-speech and ten post, NFP, PPI and CPI closed on their own ladders, and FOMC, VIX expiry and quad witching all beyond the ten-day horizon cap, a price-state sweep is the only honest search mode. What was genuinely new today was the month turn, and the one form of it this repo has never measured is the ME-0 close to ME+1 open OVERNIGHT return, since all five prior month-end closures were close-to-close. That object turned out to be real and to have the wrong mechanism attached: the headline is SPY +10.48 bp against +2.98 unconditional at sign p 0.0004, but the reversal regression the auction story predicts runs BACKWARDS on the very session that has the auction (slope +0.194 on ME-0 against -0.131 on all sessions), and the fifteen-name reference class puts EEM and EFA first and second, two markets that are shut while the US auction prints and reopen overnight in Asia and Europe. It is one market-wide overnight drift wearing fifteen labels, August is the worst of its twelve months on every vehicle, and August in a midterm year is 3-3. The 15-minute intraday cache was used by a pitch check for the first time in this product's life to test that mechanism at its own resolution, and it agreed: the ME-0 last hour is genuinely distinguishable on SPY and IWM (welch t -2.52 and -4.35) and carries 30% of session volume, but as a trade it decays monotonically and flips negative from 2018. The closest thing to a survivor was silver. The whole metals complex broke on Friday, GLD -3.24%, SLV -4.38% and GDX -3.90%, all inside the -2% rung, so the short-SLV continuation cell fired for entry today; it passed gate attribution outright, passed its local control at welch t +2.21 and posted a 67-52 record at sign p 0.019 scored against silver's own down-rate, and it still died because the effect has no shape a continuation story can produce. Entered on the signal close it pays +0.039%, one session later +0.516%, two sessions later +0.035%; and it pays MORE when silver bounces on the entry day (+0.867% on 28-15) than when it keeps falling, which falsifies the deleveraging mechanism with its own data. Shrunk toward its confirming six-family reference class the honest magnitude is 3.7x cost against a 5x bar. Two method findings are worth more than any of the candidates: a percentile computed inclusive of its own observation and one computed exclusive of it differ by enough to move a parked cell from +0.934% on 28-23 to +0.005% on 28-29 at the identical rung, and pitch_lab's cluster_note ranks concentration by ABSOLUTE value, so it nets a large winner against a large loser and reported silver's top-2 episodes as 3% of total when ranked by value they are 103%.

thesis: The dollar sells off into FOMC announcements and gets that discount back over the following week, and the post-decision tape is priced as if the announcement-day move were information. Across 212 scheduled decisions since 2000 the DX index fell on the announcement session itself (tdom-matched t -2.96, negative in all three eras), then rose 0.212% over the next five sessions against a trading-day-of-month control. The other side is short-dollar positioning put on to collect the documented announcement-day currency premium (Mueller, Tahbaz-Salehi and Vedolin) and taken off once the uncertainty resolves. It is specific to the Fed: the same five-session construction after CPI, NFP and PPI release closes pays -0.04%, +0.04% and -0.09%. It came out of a search (this morning's pre-specified short-dollar version died on a wrong-signed parent), so it is graded B, sized to one five-session standard deviation, and expressed in futures because UUP's round trip eats too much of the live-state edge.

evidence.summary: Long DX-Y.NYB from the FOMC decision close over 212 scheduled decisions: h=5 +0.212% tdom-matched excess (t 3.02, raw +0.183%, 58.5% hit, sign p 0.002), h=3 +0.172%. Charged for the 30-cell search that produced it (3 vehicles x 2 signs x h1-5), a tdom-preserving date permutation of the family max |t| gives p 0.011 at h=5; minP over the gate rungs with n >= 30 gives 0.030, over all eight rungs 0.079. Placebo ladder k=-5..+5 ranks the decision close 2 of 11 and every pre-event rung sits at or below +0.003%. Top two episodes carry 18% of the total. Edge is 14x a ~1.5 bp futures round trip on the full sample.
evidence.control: trading-day-of-month matched non-FOMC dates (mandatory for an FX event cell); reference class of CPI, NFP and PPI release closes; placebo offsets k=-5..+5
evidence.era_note: Pre-2008 is flat (h=3 +0.077%, t 0.71); 2008-17 +0.210%; 2018+ +0.214% at h=3 and +0.380% at h=5 (N 68, t 3.43). Midterm years h=5 +0.346%. 2026 so far 2-3 at -0.059% (h=3). Mechanism is half verified: the announcement-session discount is real, but its size does not predict each meeting's own rebound (slope +0.11, t 0.99), so this is an average premium unwinding rather than a meeting-by-meeting reversal.
